summary: The Indian threat picture this month is pulled in two directions at once: high-volume, financially-motivated mobile fraud hitting citizens at scale, and patient, state-aligned intrusion aimed at government, defence and critical infrastructure. The common seam is the edge — VPNs, firewalls and cloud identity — which is where ransomware crews and espionage actors alike still get their first foothold.

items.title: Fake-APK UPI fraud has gone industrial
items.why: This is no longer lone scammers. Organised networks now run fake RTO / e-challan, bank and utility APKs end to end: a single Mumbai bust was linked to 3,206 complaints and roughly ₹43 crore, and Ahmedabad police separately broke up a Telegram storefront that sold the apps to about 400 fraudsters. Individual losses keep surfacing too, such as two Pune residents who lost over ₹14 lakh to the same e-challan lure. Cash-out is fast and hard to trace (ATM withdrawals in the Ahmedabad case), and the malware (GhostBat RAT and kin) intercepts OTPs and banking SMS and captures the UPI PIN through a fake payment screen. For any payments operator, this is the live, high-volume threat, not a future one.

evidence.supports: Mumbai network: 3,206 complaints, ~₹43 crore, OTP and banking-SMS interception

items.title: The edge is still the way in
items.why: The India-relevant watchlist is dominated by internet-facing edge: Ivanti Connect Secure, Citrix NetScaler, PAN-OS and Fortinet, plus SharePoint (CVE-2025-53770, EPSS ~100%, ransomware-linked). These are the products Indian enterprises expose to the internet, and CISA lists known ransomware use for several of them, from Ivanti (CVE-2025-22457) and NetScaler (CVE-2025-5777) to PAN-OS (CVE-2026-0257) and FortiOS (CVE-2024-55591). If you do one thing this month, make it edge patch cadence: it is the single highest-leverage control on this list.

items.title: Pakistan-nexus espionage is persistent, not episodic
items.why: Transparent Tribe (APT36) and SideCopy continue to target Indian government, defence, education and research with Crimson RAT and the ZIP→LNK→LOLBin delivery pattern. These are not one-off campaigns; they are a standing collection effort that re-tools faster than it disappears. If you sit in gov, defence or academia, assume you are in scope and detect for the delivery chain, not just the final implant.

evidence.supports: Targets Indian government, defence and education; Crimson RAT; LNK and document lures

items.title: Identity is the new perimeter: watch M365 sign-ins
items.why: Microsoft and the UK NCSC reported in April 2026 that Forest Blizzard (APT28) changed DNS settings on compromised home and small-office routers to put adversary-in-the-middle servers in front of Outlook on the web, where passwords and login tokens can be intercepted. As Indian organisations move onto M365 / Entra, staff home routers become part of the attack surface. Entra sign-in risk is the signal to wire up first; Microsoft's guidance points to its risky sign-in detections. The tracker's Entra rule (high-risk successful sign-in) and its endpoint DNS rule are complementary investigation leads, not a detection of this chain: they fire separately and are not correlated, the Entra rule does not verify the MFA sequence, and a hijacked router hands out its resolver through DHCP, which the endpoint DNS rule deliberately ignores. Phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys / FIDO2) is the control that breaks the relay.

evidence.title: Microsoft Threat Intelligence: SOHO router compromise leads to DNS hijacking and adversary-in-the-middle attacks (7 Apr 2026)
evidence.supports: Forest Blizzard router DNS hijacking, AiTM against Outlook on the web, Entra risk guidance

evidence.title: NCSC: APT28 exploit routers to enable DNS hijacking operations (7 Apr 2026)

items.title: China-nexus pre-positioning in the power sector
items.why: RedEcho's targeting of load dispatch centres is about access held for later, not immediate disruption — lower tempo, higher stakes. This is the kind of intrusion that matters in a crisis rather than a quarterly report, and it belongs on the radar of anyone defending Indian critical infrastructure even when nothing is visibly happening.
